pl-l3d25c1-d1e115.summary: Announces the new topic: the sufficiency of faith for salvation.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e118.summary: For those before and after Christ's coming, faith seems to have progressed with time, as knowledge did; faith is called great by knowledge and number of articles, or by constancy and devotion. There is a measure of faith without which there was never salvation: Hebrews 11:6, one approaching God must believe that he exists and rewards those who hope in him.
claims: Faith progressed over time along with knowledge.
Faith is great either by knowledge and number of articles or by constancy and devotion.
There is a minimal measure of faith necessary for salvation at every time.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e124.summary: Asks whether this minimal belief sufficed for salvation before Christ's coming or before the Law, noting that in the time of grace it certainly does not suffice, since everything contained in the creeds must be believed.
claims: In the time of grace, believing only God's existence and reward does not suffice.
All contents of the creeds must now be believed.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e128.summary: Argues it did not suffice even before the Law or the coming, since saints' authorities testify that no one was ever saved without faith in the Mediator.
claims: Faith in the Mediator has always been necessary for salvation.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e131.summary: Augustine to Optatus: sound faith holds that no one, adult or infant, is freed from the contagion of death and the bond of original sin except through the one Mediator, Christ Jesus; the just before the incarnation were saved by believing he would come. Their faith and ours is the same, and the saying that there is no other name under heaven applies from the time humanity was corrupted in Adam.
claims: No one is freed from original sin except through Christ the Mediator.
The just before the incarnation were saved by faith in Christ to come.
The faith of the ancients and our faith are the same.
Salvation through Christ alone holds from Adam's fall onward.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e155.summary: Augustine: no one is freed from the damnation incurred through Adam except through faith in Jesus Christ.
claims: Freedom from Adamic damnation comes only through faith in Christ.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e161.summary: Augustine: the same faith in the Mediator that saves us saved the ancient just, small and great, for as we believe Christ came, died, rose, and will come to judge, they believed he would come, die, rise, and come to judge.
claims: The same faith saves ancients and moderns.
The ancients believed in the future birth, death, resurrection, and judgment; we believe them as past (except judgment).

pl-l3d25c1-d1e167.summary: Gregory on Ezekiel: those going before and following Christ crying 'Hosanna' signify that all the elect, in Judaea or now in the Church, believed and believe in the Mediator of God and humanity.
claims: All the elect, before and after Christ, believe in the Mediator.

pl-l3d25c1-d1e179.summary: Concludes that these testimonies clearly teach that salvation was never granted except through faith in the Mediator; hence one approaching God must believe what Hebrews states, but that alone does not suffice.
claims: Salvation has never been granted except through faith in the Mediator.
Belief that God exists and rewards is necessary but insufficient.

pl-l3d25c1.summary: Turns to the sufficiency of faith for salvation and the faith of the ancients. Faith has progressed over time in knowledge and number of articles. Hebrews 11:6 sets a minimal measure (believing that God exists and rewards), but in the time of grace the whole Creed must be believed, and patristic authorities (Augustine, Gregory) show that no one, before or after Christ's coming, was saved without faith in the Mediator, the ancients believing in his future coming, death, resurrection, and judgment as we believe them past. Thus the Hebrews minimum is necessary but not sufficient.
claims: Faith has progressed through history in knowledge and in the number of articles.
There is a measure of faith without which salvation was never possible.
In the time of grace, everything in the creeds must be believed.
No one, before or after the incarnation, has been saved without faith in the Mediator.
The faith of the ancient just and our faith are the same, differing in tense.
Believing that God exists and rewards is necessary but not sufficient for salvation.
